newsitem.title: USA: Dole says he has cabinet members in mind.
newsitem.headline: Dole says he has cabinet members in mind.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole said Monday he did not push harder on the character issue in the presidental debate because he did not want to wallow in President Clinton's troubles.

In a wide-ranging interview to inaugurate the new Fox News Channel, Dole also said he has had discussions with several people, including retired Joint Chiefs of Staff chairman General Colin Powell, "in a general way" about serving in his Cabinet should he be elected.
Other names he mentioned were former Secretary of Education William Bennett and former Secretary of State James Baker.

Asked if Powell would be his Secretary of State, Dole said: "I haven't made that specific promise but what I might do is indicate some of the people that would be in a Dole administration without any specific titles."
Dole said he did not press harder on the character issue in the debate because "I wasn't about to wallow in Whitewater or any of the other personal issues."
After mentioning Clinton's broken promise on a middle class tax cut, he said: "There is more to character than getting into all the personal things."

Dole also said the retirement age might have to be raised at some future date in order to save the Social Security pension system and he repeated his call for a bi-partisan commission to save the Medicare system.
Interviewer Catherine Crier asked Dole, who played a key role in the 1983 plan that saved Social Security by raising the retirement age, if he would consider doing that again.
"I don't see anything wrong with it but you got to protect the people in the pipeline. You can't have a surprise party for them ... by saying by the way you got to work six more years."

Dole gave no specifics on what he would do in terms of raising the retirement issue and his press spokesman, Nelson Warfield, said Dole was not making any proposal on an issue he has spoken about extensively in the past. Warfield said he was simply taking part in a discussion.
